clue.text: Frequently t-t- …

parts.note: the stammered letters show one t following another t

explanation.surface: A stutter that keeps repeating its first letter, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the picture aloud: t, then t again, i.e. t after t; with t standing for time, that gives the phrase. The ellipsis carries the sense on into 8 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for repeatedly, again and again, so it matches frequently.

clue.text: Maybe Flatley pranced a pirouette on table-top

parts.note: the top of the word table is its first letter
taken as written

indicators.note: a pirouette spins round, so the letters of pranced and a are spun into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous Irish dancer twirling across the top of a table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places T at the head of the anagram of PRANCED A. Michael Flatley is the Irish dancer behind Riverdance and Lord of the Dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Flatley is a celebrated percussive stepdancer, an example of the type, signalled by Maybe.

clue.text: Drug to transform extremes of insomnia

parts.note: to morph is to change shape or transform

indicators.note: extremes are the two outer letters of the word insomnia

explanation.surface: A medicine that changes a sleepless night at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for morphine, the opiate painkiller, so it is a drug.

clue.text: See 1
Stirring hint of nectarine in a weak gin — uncouth!

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the rearranged letters
uncouth means rough and unpolished, so the letters of a weak gin are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a hint is just the first letter of nectarine

explanation.surface: A rough cocktail of weak gin with a touch of nectarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncouth' rearranges A WEAK GIN to AWAKEGIN, and 'in' puts the N from nectarine inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring as a noun means rousing from sleep, a synonym of coming to.

clue.text: Receptacle for bookies' takings?

parts.note: the tote is the totalisator, a betting pool system, so a bag for its takings plays on a shopping bag's name

explanation.surface: Wondering what a bookmaker keeps the day's money in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tote is the British state-founded pool betting operator; the answer is in fact a large open shopping bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A large carry-all bag is a receptacle, and its first word is also the name of a betting system.

clue.text: Ortolans, etc, evenly cooked

indicators.note: evenly picks the letters in the even positions, second, fourth and so on, of Ortolans etc

explanation.surface: Small songbirds and the like, all cooked to the same degree.
explanation.walkthrough: Ortolans are small songbirds once eaten as a delicacy in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast meat or game is to cook it in an oven, so roasted food has been cooked.

clue.text: See 1
Flaxen curls we do hate on daughter

indicators.note: curls twist the letters of we do hate round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that they loathe the curls on their daughter's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts D after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tow is pale flax fibre, so a person with tow-coloured hair is fair-haired, flaxen.

clue.text: Peer underground to check amount of radiation

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or contain, so the resistance word holds the unit inside

parts.note: the maquis was the French resistance movement in the Second World War, an underground
R stands for roentgen, a unit measuring an amount of radiation

explanation.surface: Someone looking down a mine to measure radiation levels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb meaning look, but it is the noun for a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman ranking above an earl, a member of the peerage.

clue.text: … turducken, for instance, is warmed up (or not) at spread

indicators.note: spread out, the letters of warmed up or not at are laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stuffed festive bird dish, reheated or not, served at a buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: Turducken (turkey + duck + chicken) is both a dish of stuffed birds and a blend of three words; 'spread' looks like a meal but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend word formed from parts of others is an example of this coinage, as turducken shows.

clue.text: Stick notice in Telegraph Puzzles?

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
the puzzle pages of the Telegraph are where the solver is, here

explanation.surface: Pinning a notice in the newspaper's puzzle section.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the self-reference: you are reading this clue in the Telegraph's puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain attached, a synonym of the verb stick.

clue.text: Coax first of calves away from toxic plant

indicators.note: away from tells us to remove the letter from the plant's name

parts.note: the buttercup is a meadow flower that is poisonous to livestock

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of calves

explanation.surface: Keeping a young calf away from a poisonous weed in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to flatter someone to win them over, a synonym of coax.

clue.text: Tasteful China tea? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary says to take the two words the other way round, tea then China

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
Ming was a Chinese dynasty, famed for its porcelain

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cup of China tea is a sophisticated choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and tasteful both describe something pleasing and elegant, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Censure about lash-up with Queen creates stress

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for censure goes round the rest

parts.note: to rate is an old verb for scold or censure

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for lash reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to lash is to tie or bind
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Criticism of a botched job involving the monarch causes tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for lash in this down clue. 'lash-up' looks like a makeshift job but splits into lash plus the reversal signal; RATE as censure is an old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to say it again for emphasis, to repeat.

clue.text: Perversion follows a dismal passage

indicators.note: a passage is a short extract, here a run of letters taken from inside follows a dismal

explanation.surface: A deviant act that follows a dreary piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking pleasure in inflicting pain is a sexual or moral perversion.

clue.text: Climbing mountains, clamber over group leader displaying …

indicators.note: in a down clue over means sitting above the next letter
climbing in a down clue means the word for mountains reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Alps are the European mountain range
to shin up is to clamber

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of group

explanation.surface: A climber scaling peaks, scrambling over the head of the party, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 14 Down: splashing a fatal lapse means showing it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash something is to display it showily, as a newspaper splashes a story.

clue.text: … fatal lapse with mistral on changing course

indicators.note: a wind changing course shifts direction, so the letters of mistral on are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fatal error as the mistral, a cold wind of southern France, shifts direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a grave wrong that damns the soul, so a lapse that is fatal to it.

clue.text: Having a tiff in a skiff?

definitions.meaning: having a tiff means quarrelling, a slang sense rhyming with cow
in a skiff you would be pulling at the oars

explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling means quarrelling when said to rhyme with cow and pulling oars when said to rhyme with go.

clue.text: Note needed in old college song? Blow me!

indicators.note: needed in puts the note letter inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
N, for north, is a compass point, here the note

explanation.surface: An old student song with a missing note, and an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow me!' looks like a cry of astonishment but is the instrument speaking: it is played by blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped wind instrument, played by blowing, as if it invites you to blow it.

clue.text: Buffet guy in Basra with detonation

indicators.note: the word for guy goes inside the scattered city letters
a detonation blows things apart, so the letters of Basra are blown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a lad is a guy, a young man

explanation.surface: A man caught in a bomb blast in the Iraqi city of Basra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detonation' scatters the city's letters to SABAR before the guy goes in. 'Buffet' looks like a blow but is the self-service meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service counter of salads is a kind of buffet.

clue.text: I shall replace last 25% of sweet courses

indicators.note: shall replace says the letter I takes the place of the closing quarter, the last two of eight letters

parts.note: a syllabub is a creamy dessert, a sweet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to swap the last part of a dessert course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last 25% of' names the final two of the eight letters of SYLLABUB, UB, which I replaces. 'courses' looks like meal courses but means study programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural of syllabus, the outlines of subjects in programmes of study, i.e. courses.

clue.text: Wrap up books — one on pronunciation

indicators.note: on places the number letter next to the pronunciation word

parts.note: a burr is a rough regional pronunciation, especially of the letter r
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down clue up turns the books abbreviation to read from bottom to top

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: Packing books away, with one note on how a word is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' looks like the definition, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay, turning the books abbreviation round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla wrapped round a filling is a kind of wrap, a Mexican food.

clue.text: Insurgent penetrates renowned computer plant

indicators.note: penetrates means gets inside, so the insurgent goes into the computer's name

parts.note: HAL is the famous computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey
an insurgent is a rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel hacker breaking into a famous computer installation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory or installation but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild flower with blue bell-shaped blooms, also called the bluebell of Scotland, so a plant.

clue.text: Artistic support starts in early at school, expanding later

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters of early, at, school, expanding and later

explanation.surface: Art education that begins early at school and broadens later on.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden stand that holds a painter's canvas, literally supporting the artist's work.

clue.text: Elite mountaineer, after French pulled back, bagging Himalayan peak

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the reversed French word holds the letter inside
pulled back means the French word is read backwards

parts.note: apres is French for after

indicators.note: a peak is a top, here the first letter of Himalayan

explanation.surface: A climber who, after a French team retreated, conquered a Himalayan summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled back' turns APRES into SERPA, which takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan people famed as expert high-altitude guides and porters, top mountaineers.

clue.text: Three measures activists list at gathering

indicators.note: gathering pulls together the letters of activists list at into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Campaigners drawing up a list at a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful term for a person's bust, waist and hip sizes, three body measurements.

clue.text: Unconventional instruction on tablets for stomach?

definitions.meaning: a label telling you to swallow the pills while reclining would be an odd dosing direction
to stomach something is to tolerate or put up with it

explanation.surface: An odd direction on a pill packet for a stomach complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning to accept something without protest, i.e. tolerate it.
